analysis.investment_thesis: Park Medi World operates NABH-accredited multi-specialty hospitals in NCR riding India's healthcare boom, but at 44x P/E with net profit CAGR of only 3.3% over four years, the market is pricing in perfection that the financials simply do not support. Revenue growth (16.1% CAGR) is not converting to earnings — finance costs ballooning 26.3% CAGR and margin compression make this a story I cannot buy at this price.
key_strengths: Good ROE/ROCE of 21.2%/20.4% — capital employed is generating reasonable returns
High promoter holding at 82.89% signals skin-in-the-game and alignment with minority shareholders
Revenue growing at a solid 16.1% CAGR with NABH-accredited multi-super-specialty brand in high-purchasing-power NCR market
key_risks: Earnings barely growing — net profit CAGR of only 3.3% vs revenue CAGR of 16.1%; net margin collapsed from 24.4% (FY21) to 15.3% (FY25)
Finance costs surging 26.3% CAGR (₹24 Cr → ₹61 Cr); borrowings more than doubled to ₹734 Cr — debt burden is eating the growth story
Valuation demands growth that isn't materialising — at 44x P/E and FCF of only ₹66 Cr on ₹9,350 Cr market cap, FCF yield is a meagre 0.7%
red_flags: Net profit in FY24 crashed to ₹152 Cr from ₹228 Cr in FY23 — a 33% drop mid-expansion cycle is alarming
Operating cash flow is highly volatile (₹223 Cr → ₹155 Cr → ₹199 Cr → ₹361 Cr → ₹191 Cr) — quality of earnings is suspect
FII ownership at only 0.86% despite being in the marquee healthcare sector signals institutional investors are unconvinced at these levels
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Park Medi World is a legitimate healthcare business — NABH-accredited, multi-specialty, operating in Gurugram which is one of India's wealthiest catchments. The 60.85% gross margin confirms pricing power at the unit level, and ROE above 20% is respectable. However, the fundamental problem is that the company is growing its top line at 16% while debt costs are growing at 26.3% — meaning every rupee of incremental revenue is increasingly going to service lenders, not shareholders. The net profit in FY25 (₹213 Cr) is only 14% above FY21 (₹187 Cr) over four years. That is not the compounding machine I want to own.

The valuation is the final nail. At 44x P/E and EV/EBITDA of 22x, this stock is priced like an Apollo Hospitals or Max Healthcare — category leaders with pan-India networks, strong brands, and demonstrated earnings compounding. Park Medi World is a regional player with ₹1,394 Cr in revenues and inconsistent free cash flow (₹66 Cr in FY25 vs ₹294 Cr in FY24). Capex jumped to ₹159 Cr in FY25 with CWIP rising to ₹54 Cr, suggesting expansion is underway — but execution risk is real when the balance sheet is already carrying ₹734 Cr in borrowings. I would revisit if earnings growth re-accelerates meaningfully and the stock corrects to sub-25x P/E.
